questions.q: What were some of Jesus’ disciples doing that offended the Pharisees and scribes?
questions.a: Some of the disciples were eating with unwashed hands.

questions.q: Whose tradition was it that hands, cups, pots, and copper vessels be washed before eating?
questions.a: It was the tradition of the elders that hands, cups, pots, and copper vessels be washed before eating.

questions.q: What did Jesus say to the Pharisees and scribes about their teaching on the issue of washing?
questions.a: Jesus said that the Pharisees and scribes taught the rules of men while abandoning the commandment of God.

questions.q: How did the Pharisees and scribes void the commandment of God which says to honor your father and mother?
questions.a: They voided God’s commandment by telling people to give to them as Corban the money that would have helped their father and mother.

questions.q: What did Jesus say does not defile a person?
questions.a: Jesus said that nothing from outside of a person can defile him when it enters into him.

questions.q: What did Jesus say defiles a person?
questions.a: Jesus said that what comes out of a person defiles him.

questions.q: What did Jesus say does not defile a person?
questions.a: Jesus said that nothing from outside of a person can defile him when it enters into him.

questions.q: What kinds of foods did Jesus declare to be clean?
questions.a: Jesus declared all foods to be clean.

questions.q: What did Jesus say defiles a person?
questions.a: Jesus said that what comes out of a person defiles him.

questions.q: What are three things that Jesus said can come out of a person to defile him?
questions.a: Jesus said that evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery, coveting, wickedness, deceit, sensuality, envy, slander, pride, and folly can come out of a person to defile him.

questions.q: Was the woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit a Jew or a Greek?
questions.a: The woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit was a Greek.

questions.q: How did the woman respond when Jesus told her that it was not right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs?
questions.a: The woman said that even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.

questions.q: What did Jesus do for the woman?
questions.a: Jesus cast the demon out of the woman’s daughter.

questions.q: When the man who was deaf and had a speech impediment was brought to Jesus, what did he do to heal him?
questions.a: Jesus put his fingers in the man’s ears, spit and touched his tongue, then looked to heaven and said, “Open!”

questions.q: What did the people do when Jesus told them to tell no one about his healings?
questions.a: The more Jesus commanded them to be quiet, the more they talked about it.

commentary.text: The woman of Canaan's daughter cured.
Christ restores a man to hearing and speech.

Verses 1–13 One great design of Christ's coming was, to set aside the ceremonial law; and to make way for this, he rejects the ceremonies men added to the law of God's making. Those clean hands and that pure heart which Christ bestows on his disciples, and requires of them, are very different from the outward and superstitious forms of Pharisees of every age. Jesus reproves them for rejecting the commandment of God. It is clear that it is the duty of children, if their parents are poor, to relieve them as far as they are able; and if children deserve to die that curse their parents, much more those that starve them. But if a man conformed to the traditions of the Pharisees, they found a device to free him from the claim of this duty.

Our wicked thoughts and affections, words and actions, defile us, and these only. As a corrupt fountain sends forth corrupt streams, so does a corrupt heart send forth corrupt reasonings, corrupt appetites and passions, and all the wicked words and actions that come from them. A spiritual understanding of the law of God, and a sense of the evil of sin, will cause a man to seek for the grace of the Holy Spirit, to keep down the evil thoughts and affections that work within.

Christ never put any from him that fell at his feet, which a poor trembling soul may do. As she was a good woman, so a good mother. This sent her to Christ. His saying, Let the children first be filled, shows that there was mercy for the Gentiles, and not far off. She spoke, not as making light of the mercy, but magnifying the abundance of miraculous cures among the Jews, in comparison with which a single cure was but as a crumb. Thus, while proud Pharisees are left by the blessed Saviour, he manifests his compassion to poor humbled sinners, who look to him for children's bread. He still goes about to seek and save the lost.

Here is a cure of one that was deaf and dumb. Those who brought this poor man to Christ, besought him to observe the case, and put forth his power. Our Lord used more outward actions in the doing of this cure than usual. These were only signs of Christ's power to cure the man, to encourage his faith, and theirs that brought him. Though we find great variety in the cases and manner of relief of those who applied to Christ, yet all obtained the relief they sought. Thus it still is in the great concerns of our souls.
